items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: I loved him after that, because my wife and I needed the money.

ctx.x: they didn't -- well I had a tuxedo, but no one told me tuxedo, so I grabbed my trumpet and a dark suit and I ran on down there. So I got ready to get on the stand and the manager who ran the place, somebody, said Who are you?

I said I'm the trumpet player. Well where's your tux? I said well nobody told me to. He said well you can't get up on -- you can't get up there, you know. Well, I figure speak for four or five dollars (unintelligible) you know. Until you get the tux you can't get on that stand. Maybe he was waiter. I don't know who the heck he was. Pops walks in there, and I sat back there alone. What's the matter, boy? What's the matter, fellow? Huh? this man says I can't get up, I says (unintelligible). Why can't -- why --…
Because he was with the big band there making money,
